subject.title: Parent sessions operate on stale child state when humans interact with child or ACP sessions directly

question: Should the first implementation expose retained typed session history, or limit v1 to durable session versions and parent invalidation?
rationale: The central stale-parent problem only requires durable version and invalidation, while retained history adds substantial permanent storage and model-facing semantics that current repository behavior does not settle.

options.title: Version-first v1
options.body: Persist session heads and watcher cursors, recover outstanding notices after restart, and defer retained typed history until a concrete consumer requires it.

options.title: Full history v1
options.body: Implement the proposed event-kind union, retention, history-gap behavior, and changesSince tool output immediately.

options.title: No coherence guarantee
options.body: Keep run-completion announcements as the only parent update path and document that direct child interaction may leave parents stale.

recommendation.title: Version-first v1
recommendation.body: Persist session heads and watcher cursors, recover outstanding notices after restart, and defer retained typed history until a concrete consumer requires it.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest history-backed owner for the current system-event, lifecycle, status, and shared-state surfaces and authored this protected design issue.
